transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess what brought me in is that I kind of went from being a regular crew guy to trying to do everything at once. I was running three bids, calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, messaging everybody I knew about this park idea… it was like I couldn’t shut it off.
During that time, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I was sleeping weird, but I can’t say for sure that I needed way less sleep. I just know I was up late a lot because my mind was still going.
During that time, did you hear or see things that other people didn’t?
No, I don’t think so. I wasn’t seeing things or hearing voices or anything like that. It was more like my head was just really busy.
During that time, did you feel unusually confident or important, like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yeah… I did. At the time I really thought I was about to become, like, the main guy every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping. Looking back, that sounds pretty big, because I’m still just trying to keep my small jobs paid up, but in that moment I believed it.
During that time, were you talking a lot more than usual or feeling like you couldn't stop talking?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember people saying I was talking nonstop or anything. I might’ve been more wound up in conversations, but I can’t say I couldn’t stop talking.
During that time, were you hospitalized because of how you were acting or feeling?
No, I wasn’t hospitalized for it. It got bad, but I didn’t end up in the hospital.
Were you using methamphetamine, cocaine, Adderall, or other stimulants around that time?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t have anything specific like that to point to from then.
During that time, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah, kind of. Before I crashed, I felt really fired up, like almost bigger than myself. Not just happy exactly—more amped up. And if someone at work questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them way harder than I should’ve.
During that time, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or with other people?

Yeah, it’s started causing problems at work. I’ve been missing details on bids and measurements, stuff I normally wouldn’t mess up. And in landscaping, that can turn into a big deal fast. I’m worried one bad mistake could cost me clients or even get someone hurt on a job site.
About how many days in a row did that fired-up, amped-up period last?
I’d say it was about two weeks straight. It started when I got really caught up in remaking myself for that park pitch, and then after those couple weeks I just kind of crashed.
After that two-week fired-up period ended, did you go into a stretch where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah. After that ended, I dropped pretty hard. I’ve been feeling depressed like that most days for… honestly about a year now, but this latest crash has been the worst it’s gotten.
During that fired-up period, were you doing a lot more goal-directed activity than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I went from just being a normal crew guy to trying to do all this extra stuff at once—running like three bids, calling city people, trying to line up plant suppliers, messaging everybody I knew about the park idea. It was like I couldn’t shut it off.
During that fired-up two-week period, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?
Yeah, they did. My head was just going constantly — plant lists, slogans, layouts for the park, who I needed to talk to or impress. I’d fill up pages in a notebook and still feel like I was behind.
During that fired-up period, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

Yeah… I spent money like it was already guaranteed to come back. I put tools, plants, work clothes, even ads on a credit card. At the time it felt like it made sense, like I was investing in it, but now I look at the balance and I feel sick because I can’t cover it.
Before this two-week fired-up period, had you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually energized or revved up in a similar way?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt motivated or worked extra hard, but I don’t know if it was like this. This one felt different enough that it stands out.
Before this recent two-week fired-up period, had there ever been another time in your life when you felt revved up or unusually energized in a similar way?
I don’t think so. I’ve had stretches where I was working hard or felt more motivated, but not really revved up like that. This last one is the only time I can point to where it felt that intense.
